newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KNP BT SAYS FIRST QUARTER DISAPPOINTING.
newsitem.headline: KNP BT SAYS FIRST QUARTER DISAPPOINTING.

text.p: Dutch paper, packaging and office products group KNP BT said on Wednesday results in the first quarter of this year were disappointing.
"Given business in the first two months, first quarter results will probably be slightly lower than in the year-ago period," KNP BT said in a statement.
In February, the company said it expected earnings from operations to improve in 1997 after fourth quarter and full-year profits fell sharply last year.
"But we maintain our expectation that the 1997 profit from ordinary operations will substantially improve compared with 1996, provided that the paper market does not deteriorate," KNP BT said.
KNP BT said its distribution division had a good influx of orders in the first quarter of the current year but sales at the graphic systems division lagged behind last year's.
This could be partly offset by the paper merchanting and office products divisions, it added.
KNP BT's packaging units posted lower profits than in the first quarter of 1996, mainly as a result of lower prices of corrugated cardboard paper.
Results at majority-owned paper maker KNP Leykam were depressed as the start of a rebuilt production unit in the Netherlands took longer than expected, KNP said.
Last month, KNP BT said its 1996 net profit from ordinary operations more than halved to 231 million guilders from 545 million in 1995.
In the fourth quarter of last year, the company's net profit from ordinary operations plunged to 92 million guilders from 1995's 151 million.
